C++.justification: `f(x)` bare call, `x` a std::vector<int> passed with no sigil — plainest ordinary call-site form.

Go.justification: Bare call f(x) with x a slice; ordinary Go call-site syntax with no sigils.

Java.justification: Ordinary call f(x) on a List argument passes the reference by value; callee can read/write/resize elements of the same underlying object, observable through x afterward.

Kotlin.fragment:
val x = mutableListOf(1, 2, 3)
f(x)
return x[0]
Kotlin.justification: f(x) — Kotlin's ordinary call syntax has no sigils; JVM reference-passing semantics for a MutableList argument, so the callee's access is not determinable at the call site alone.

Python.fragment:
x = [1, 2, 3]
f(x)
e = x[0]
return e
Python.justification: f(x) is Python's ordinary bare call form; objects are passed by object reference per Python's evaluation model.

Quidra.citation: language.md: 'Ordinary arguments have value semantics' -- the ordinary bare call-site form f(x) is unambiguous value-passing by the language's own contract; llm-guide.md item 17.

Swift.justification: f(x) — ordinary bare call syntax; Array has value semantics (COW) so no sigil is required or available at the call site.

TypeScript.justification: f(x) bare call; JS/TS arrays are reference-semantic objects passed by reference by default at ordinary call sites.

Zig.justification: f(x) bare call — Zig has no implicit reference passing for aggregate value types at an ordinary call site; ArrayList passed by value is a struct copy of the descriptor, elements are heap-shared depending on type, expressible and buildable.
